extracted.intended_audience: authors, peer reviewers, editors, and readers of diagnostic accuracy studies (including those using AI)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and reviewing reports of diagnostic accuracy studies to ensure completeness and transparency (STARD 2015), including an AI-extension (STARD-AI) addressing algorithm-specific reporting elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD 2015 — 30 essential items
rubrics_metrics.description: STARD 2015 list now has 30 essential items identified by an international expert group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list of 30 items is intended as an essential checklist for authors, reviewers and other readers to improve completeness and transparency of diagnostic accuracy study reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help readers judge potential for bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Report items that help readers judge the potential for bias in the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reported, these items enable assessment of sources and magnitude of bias that could affect diagnostic accuracy estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appraise applicability of study findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Report items that help readers appraise the applicability of study findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient context (population, setting, test role) so readers can determine whether results apply to their clinical context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess validity of conclusions and recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Report items that help readers assess the validity of conclusions and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure methods and results are reported with enough detail and transparency to evaluate whether conclusions are supported by the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title — identify study as diagnostic accuracy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit in the title that the study is a diagnostic accuracy study so readers and indexers can identify it immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract — provide a clear summary
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a structured, clear summary of objectives, study design, participants, index test(s), reference standard, key results (accuracy estimates) and conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background — clinical role and study question
rubrics_metrics.description: Background (clinical role of test, study question).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the clinical role of the index test and state the specific study question or objective driving the accuracy evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — study design, participants, test methods, analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods (study design, participants, test methods, analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed description of study design (prospective/retrospective), participant recruitment and selection, how index test(s) and reference standard were performed and interpreted, and statistical methods used to estimate accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results — participants, test results, accuracy estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Results (participants, test results, estimates of diagnostic accuracy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report participant flow and characteristics, numbers of participants undergoing index test and reference standard, cross-tabulations of results, and accuracy measures with uncertainty (e.g., sensitivity, specificity, CIs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion — limitations, applicability, implications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss study limitations, potential sources of bias, generalizability/applicability of findings, and implications for practice and future research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other items — registration, protocol, funding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report trial or study registration details, availability of protocol, and sources of funding and role of funders to improve transparency and reduce risk of undisclosed bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD-AI — algorithm description
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the AI algorithm used (architecture, versions, hyperparameters or references) so readers can understand what was evaluated and enable reproducibility or comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD-AI — data preprocessing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report steps taken to preprocess input data (e.g., normalization, augmentation, exclusion criteria) that could affect model performance and generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD-AI — training/validation/test set composition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details on how datasets were split or sampled, number of participants/cases in each set, and whether splits were independent and representative to avoid optimistic bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD-AI — performance metrics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report which metrics were used (e.g., AUC, sensitivity/specificity, calibration measures), how they were computed, and include uncertainty estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD-AI — generalizability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address expected performance in external populations/settings, and report any external validation or domain-shift analyses to inform applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD-AI — comparison with non-AI standards
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare AI performance to existing non-AI diagnostic standards or clinical practice to contextualize added value or limitations.
